name: Seoul

supply.note: Seoul draws on the Han River through six treatment plants. No annual production figure with a year attached has been captured.

freshness_note: The water table has applied since 1 July 2021; the sewerage table since 1 January 2026, with a published schedule to 2030.
open_items: The treatment of 하수도 사용료 under Korean tax law, which holds the total water services figure and not the supply figure.
A primary designation of the ordinary residential connection size, which would lift the supply metric from Grade B to Grade A.
grade_note: Grade B, and not for a missing rate. Seoul is the cleanest tariff structure captured so far — three flat volumetric rates and one fixed charge, all under named ordinances. It is held on the two questions a rate table cannot answer: what tax sits on top, and which connection the reference household has.
resolution_note: The VAT question that withheld Seoul is closed on the supply side by statute rather than by the silence of a rate table: art. 26(1)2 of the Value-Added Tax Act exempts tap water, and Basic Ruling 26-0-1 attaches that to a supplier under the Water Supply Act. The sewerage side is a different question and stays open, so total water services is not published.
